overview: A heavy day dominated by Israel's post-election deadlock, a deadly Spanish rail crash, Cyclone Arnab's landfall on the Andhra coast, and a sharp fall in Indian markets as crude oil passed $115, with the US-Iran standoff casting a shadow over all of it.

items.headline: Israel's election leaves a coalition puzzle, with Arab parties as kingmakers and Likud alleging fraud
items.summary: Israel's parliamentary election has produced no clear route to a government, and smaller parties now hold the balance of power. Likud says the result was 'stolen' and has demanded an investigation.
items.detail: Al Jazeera and NDTV highlight Arab parties emerging as kingmakers, while Netanyahu and Gadi Eisenkot are the two names at the centre of the coalition question. The Times of Israel reports that Likud claims the election was stolen by Arab parties and wants an investigation into alleged fraud. The BBC sets out four possible scenarios for breaking the deadlock. Israel's system is based on parliamentary majorities, so whoever can assemble 61 seats in the Knesset is the one who can form a government.
items.analysis: Coalition talks and the fraud investigation will run in parallel, and the result could take weeks to settle. Watch how the Arab parties position themselves, since their support or refusal will shape the outcome.

items.headline: Cyclone Arnab hits the Andhra coast, killing at least five with damage across 10 districts
items.summary: Cyclone Arnab has battered the Andhra Pradesh coast, with The Hindu reporting five deaths and other outlets counting eight. The state has announced Rs 5 lakh ex gratia for the families of those killed.
items.detail: Reports say the storm uprooted trees and electricity poles, damaged homes, and knocked out roads and power lines across 10 districts. The Hindu's live coverage confirms the Rs 5 lakh payment to the families of the dead. Rain has eased over Keralam as the cyclone made landfall, and temperatures there are expected to rise again. Death tolls differ between outlets, so the official count may still change as damage assessments come in.
items.analysis: Cyclones on this coast often cause the most harm through flooding, falling trees and power outages, so restoration work will matter as much as the storm itself. Figures should be read as provisional until district reports are complete.

items.headline: Two trains collide in Spain's Toledo Province, with at least 64 dead
items.summary: Two trains collided in Spain's Toledo Province, and the death toll reported so far is at least 64. Reuters puts the toll higher at 68 and calls it Spain's second major train crash this year.
items.detail: Drone footage shows twisted carriages and wreckage at the site. The line involved is part of Spain's first high-speed network, and Hindustan Times reports that attention is on the systems meant to keep trains apart and on a possible error. Reuters notes that this is the second major rail disaster in Spain this year. Investigators will need to establish how the trains came to be on the same track.
items.analysis: Early focus will be on signalling and train-control systems. Repeated major crashes in one year will put pressure on rail operators and regulators to explain what has changed.

items.headline: Iran rejects Qatari peace proposal as Gulf states work on a wider deal to head off renewed US strikes
items.summary: Iran has called the latest mediation ideas unacceptable, even as Qatar says it has presented a new draft. US forces are reported to be ready to resume strikes on Iran within 96 hours, awaiting a decision from President Trump.
items.detail: A senior Iranian official told Reuters that the ideas put forward in the latest mediation were unacceptable, and Iran's Foreign Ministry said a Qatari delegation had visited Tehran. Qatari mediators say they presented a new draft deal. NDTV, citing reports, says US forces are ready to renew strikes within 96 hours. The WSJ reports that US officials warned Gulf countries of a possible short, intense renewal of the war after the US midterms. Trump has said Iran wants a deal but that negotiations have been delayed. The Guardian reports that Gulf states are working on a multipart deal aimed at preventing a return to fighting.
items.analysis: The conflict has already killed Indian nationals, according to the Indian government, and energy prices react sharply to every signal. The next few days will show whether the Gulf mediation can close the gap or whether military options move forward.

items.headline: Bolsonaro's son leaves Brazil for the US after Lula's election win
items.summary: Flavio Bolsonaro, who lost Brazil's presidential election to Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, has landed in Miami. The US State Department says he and his family will receive US visas.
items.detail: Al Jazeera and The Guardian report his arrival in Miami, though one Indian outlet had earlier reported a flight to Ecuador. AP reports that the State Department confirmed visas for him and his family. Lula's win is being read by commentators as going against a rightward tide in Latin America, and The Indian Express argues that the result stands out in the region. Some analysts link Brazil's position to the wider US approach in Latin America.
items.analysis: The episode puts the spotlight on how Washington engages with Brazil and the region, a question Brazil's government has framed around strategic autonomy. Whether the Bolsonaro family's move affects the political right in Brazil is still open.

items.headline: Russia hosts Africa summit in Moscow, pitching a 'multipolar world order'
items.summary: Russia is hosting a summit with African leaders in Moscow, presenting itself as a partner for a more multipolar world. Al Jazeera has set out the agenda and why the meeting matters.
items.detail: The New Indian Express reports that Russia is courting African leaders with the idea of a multipolar world order, in which power is spread across several centres rather than concentrated in the West. Al Jazeera has explained the agenda, though the headlines do not list specific agreements. Russia has sought to expand political and economic ties in Africa, particularly since its falling out with Western governments over Ukraine, and summits like this are one way it does so.
items.analysis: The value of the summit will depend on concrete commitments rather than rhetoric. It also fits a wider competition for influence in Africa among Russia, China, the West and Gulf states.

items.headline: Gas prices and the Iran war loom over the US midterm elections
items.summary: Fuel prices have become a central theme before the US midterms, with one analysis calling the gas price the most important number in American politics. Democrats are discussing investigations they could launch if they win control of Congress.
items.detail: EnergyNow argues that gas prices are shaping voter attitudes. The BBC has outlined four investigations Democrats could launch if they take control of Congress, while The Conversation reports that Republicans are on the back foot ahead of the vote. NBC is tracking congressional polls. The Guardian notes that the Federal Reserve is expected to hold interest rates steady at its last decision before the midterms. Energy prices have been pushed up by the Middle East conflict, linking the war directly to the domestic campaign.
items.analysis: Because energy costs are tied to events in the Gulf, the outcome of the Iran standoff could affect the campaign as much as anything said on the stump. Watch the polls and any change in fuel prices in the coming weeks.

items.headline: Pakistan reverses course and lets Taiwanese airlines use its airspace
items.summary: Pakistan has reversed an earlier decision and will allow Taiwanese airlines to use its airspace. The earlier move had been linked to Islamabad's One-China policy.
items.detail: Reports said Pakistan had blocked Taiwanese carriers from its airspace, a step India Today described as going further than China itself. India's Ministry of External Affairs said direct India-Taiwan flights 'will fly', according to the Times of India. Bloomberg describes the change as an abrupt U-turn. Airspace access affects flight times, fuel costs and route planning, so the decision has practical as well as political weight.
items.analysis: The reversal shows how airspace rules can become part of broader diplomatic signalling. Whether the change holds, and how other countries respond, is what to watch.

items.headline: BJP sweeps Karnataka council seats; PM Modi's jibe on ballot papers draws Congress response
items.summary: The BJP and JD(S) won all four Karnataka legislative council seats in the latest polls, leaving Congress with none. Prime Minister Modi mocked Congress over its performance, and Congress responded by daring him to commit to ballot-paper voting.
items.detail: Polls for 28 council seats were held across Karnataka, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. ThePrint reports that Congress had held 38 of the 75 seats in Karnataka's upper house before the polls, and now has fewer. In Uttar Pradesh the BJP was leading in five seats against the SP's three, with counting underway in others. Modi's remarks prompted Congress to accept the challenge to vote by ballot paper, while the BJP has used a 'trust chori' jibe. Jan Suraj opened its account in Bihar, according to Deccan Herald.
items.analysis: Legislative council members are chosen indirectly, so these results reflect party strength among legislators and local bodies rather than a direct popular vote. Both sides are using the result to frame the wider debate on electoral trust.

items.headline: INDIA bloc readies November 1 rally and a campaign against the Chief Election Commissioner
items.summary: The INDIA opposition bloc plans a rally on November 1 and a mock parliament, and wants a public impeachment of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The JD(U), a government ally, has condemned the plan.
items.detail: India Today reports that the bloc plans a mock parliament, a public campaign against the CEC and a Delhi rally. The New Indian Express quotes the CJP saying the government is 'choosing its voters', and it backs the rally. The JD(U) says Congress is insulting Parliament and the judiciary through the public impeachment plan, according to the Economic Times. The BJP's Himachal unit has meanwhile announced four 'Save Democracy' marches, accusing Congress of destabilisation. Formal removal of a CEC is a parliamentary process, so the campaign is mainly political.
items.analysis: The campaign ties the opposition's critique of electoral administration to a public event, while the government side frames it as an attack on institutions. The rally's size and reach will show how far the issue resonates.

items.headline: Apple launches M6 MacBook Pro and iMac, pitching faster on-device AI
items.summary: Apple has unveiled a new 14-inch MacBook Pro and an iMac built around its M6 chip. The company is promoting faster AI features that run directly on the device.
items.detail: Apple's launch event, which coverage called 'Pro and tell', introduced the M6 generation across its laptop and desktop lines. The pitch centres on on-device AI, meaning tasks are processed on the laptop or desktop itself rather than sent to remote servers. Apple has been building this approach for several years, arguing it can offer quicker responses and better privacy. Reviews and real-world speed tests will show how large the gains are in practice.
items.analysis: Watch whether the on-device AI features translate into noticeable everyday improvements, since that will shape how much buyers value newer chips.

items.headline: Apple says a small number of iPhone Duo inner displays are affected
items.summary: Apple has acknowledged screen problems on a small number of its foldable iPhone Duo units and says it will replace affected phones. Early user complaints about cracking screens have been reported.
items.detail: Reports from several outlets say some owners have seen their inner foldable displays crack or fail. Apple has responded that only a small number of units are affected and that it will replace those that show screen problems. Bloomberg reported early complaints, and CNBC noted the company responded to user reports. Foldable screens are a known engineering challenge because the panel must bend thousands of times without breaking.
items.analysis: The scale of the issue is not yet clear, so it is worth watching whether Apple publishes more detail on the cause or extends its replacement programme.

items.headline: China's new export curbs draw a line around its AI crown jewels
items.summary: China has introduced new export restrictions that set limits on which AI technologies can leave the country. The move signals that Beijing is treating its most advanced AI know-how as strategically sensitive.
items.detail: Reuters reports that the new curbs define which AI capabilities count as core assets that cannot be freely exported. Export controls are government rules limiting the sale or transfer of technology abroad, often for security reasons. Governments such as the United States already restrict advanced chips and chip-making tools sent to China, so China's measures reflect a similar logic in reverse. Companies working across borders may need to check whether their products or research fall under the new lines.
items.analysis: The exact scope of the controls will determine how much they affect global AI partnerships and cross-border research.

items.headline: Hackers used 44 AI agents to automate cyberattacks, researchers say
items.summary: Security researchers report that attackers used a set of 44 AI agents to automate parts of cyberattacks. The case points to AI being used to speed up and scale hacking work.
items.detail: AI agents are software programs that can carry out multi-step tasks with limited human direction. According to the NDTV report of researchers' findings, the attackers used dozens of such agents to automate parts of their operations. Security teams have long worried that AI could lower the skill needed for attacks, and this example shows how that concern is becoming concrete. Defenders are also using AI tools to detect and respond to threats, so the contest is becoming increasingly automated on both sides.
items.analysis: Organisations will likely need to pay closer attention to automated attack patterns, since they can move faster than manual intrusions.

items.headline: ISRO to launch NVS-03 navigation satellite on October 30 after changing its approach following NVS-02 failure
items.summary: ISRO plans to launch the NVS-03 navigation satellite on October 30 from Sriharikota on a GSLV-F18 rocket. The mission is meant to strengthen NavIC, India's regional navigation system, and reports say ISRO has changed its approach after an earlier setback.
items.detail: Reports say the GSLV-F18 rocket will carry NVS-03, a next-generation NavIC satellite that includes a homegrown atomic clock. NavIC is India's own satellite navigation system, designed to cover India and the region around it. India Today reports that ISRO has changed its playbook for this mission after the NVS-02 failure, though the headlines do not detail the specific fixes. A successful launch would add to the constellation that supports location and timing services across the country.
items.analysis: The outcome will show whether the changes made after the NVS-02 setback have worked, and it is a useful test of India's ability to improve its own navigation capability.

items.headline: Islands hold nearly 20% of Earth's biodiversity but are often overlooked in conservation plans
items.summary: Islands make up only about 7% of Earth's land but hold almost a fifth of its biodiversity. A new study says they still receive too little attention in global conservation strategies.
items.detail: Research summarised by Phys.org notes that island ecosystems face pressures such as sea-level rise and biological invasions, where non-native species spread and disrupt local wildlife. Many island species are found nowhere else, which makes losses there especially hard to reverse. The study argues that global biodiversity planning has not given islands enough weight relative to their importance. The researchers point to the gap between how much these ecosystems matter and how often they feature in policy.
items.analysis: It is a useful reminder that conservation priorities can miss places that are small in area but very rich in unique species.

items.headline: UN Loss and Damage Fund provisionally approves $21.6 million for flood-hit Nepal
items.summary: The UN's Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage has provisionally approved $21.6 million for Nepal, which was hit by a debris flow and flash flood in August. The decision was made at an extraordinary meeting.
items.detail: Nepal suffered a catastrophic debris flow and flash flood on August 26, and the fund's board met in an extraordinary session to consider help. The money is described as provisional, meaning it is approved in principle and details of disbursement are still to be finalised. The Loss and Damage Fund was set up to help developing countries cope with climate-related losses that they cannot avoid or fully recover from. It has received relatively little public attention compared with larger climate finance channels.
items.analysis: Watch how quickly the provisional approval becomes actual funds on the ground, since that is what determines its real impact.

items.headline: Vizhinjam fisherwomen turn otolith into delicate jewellery
items.summary: Fisherwomen in Vizhinjam, a fishing coastline in Kerala, are making delicate jewellery from otoliths, the small bony structures found in fish ears. The craft gives a new use to a material usually discarded.
items.detail: Otoliths are tiny calcium carbonate structures in the inner ear of fish, used by the fish to sense balance and movement. They are usually a by-product of processing catch and rarely have a commercial use. According to The New Indian Express, women from the Vizhinjam fishing community are shaping these pieces into jewellery. The story highlights how coastal communities can find new livelihood ideas from materials that are close at hand.
items.analysis: It is a small example of local craft turning an overlooked resource into an income source, and it may be worth following if the venture grows.
